requirements.title: Executing EXIT terminates the construct it belongs to and handles CHANGE TEAM as END TEAM transfer
requirements.definition: When EXIT belongs to a DO construct, it terminates that loop and active loops contained within it. When EXIT belongs to a non-DO construct, it terminates active loops contained within that construct and completes execution of that construct. If it belongs to CHANGE TEAM, the effect is the same as transferring control to END TEAM, with STAT= or ERRMSG= variables defined as specified for END TEAM when present.

review_rationale: batch117: independent fresh-context source review against pinned J3/24-007 (sha256 7371e889...). Reviewer read all 35 base units in the original PDF and verified the titles from the source as Purpose and form of the SELECT TYPE construct, Execution of the SELECT TYPE construct, Examples of the SELECT TYPE construct, and the EXIT statement. Verified 35 base units, 30 requirements and 89 facets, all pending, with per-section figures 15/15/43, 11/8/25, 2/0/0 and 7/7/21. The accounting claim that 18 base units are newly accounted was verified independently, together with the numbered-item asymmetry of 13 in 11.1.11.1, none in 11.1.11.2 or 11.1.11.3, and 4 in 11.1.12. The reviewer also independently confirmed that none of R1154 through R1158 or C1162 through C1173 has pre-existing cases under tests, which matters because registering a numbered rule that already has legacy fixtures structurally forces binding them and would make the packet claim execution credit without fixture review. The type-guard matching rules were derived independently from the source before comparison: a TYPE IS guard matches when the dynamic type and kind type parameter values are the same, a CLASS IS guard matches when the dynamic type is an extension of the specified type, and selection prefers TYPE IS first, then a unique CLASS IS, then among several CLASS IS guards the one specifying a type that is an extension of all the types specified in the others, then CLASS DEFAULT, then no block. That most-specific-match rule was verified word for word. Exactly one permission is registered, the 11.1.11.2 p9 internal branch to the end-select-type statement, whose only wording also supplies the paired outside-branch restriction; no processor-latitude permission exists in this scope and none was invented. The attribution table was audited including the three C1163 rows, the three C1170 rows, the C1166 split into BIND and SEQUENCE, and the C1168 and C1172 readings, both of which were confirmed correct: C1168 does not prohibit one TYPE IS together with one CLASS IS of the same type, and C1172 is not a blanket ban on a textual EXIT inside DO CONCURRENT but turns on which construct the EXIT belongs to. The ownership boundary against 11.1.3.3 was checked in both directions, with this packet owning SELECT TYPE syntax, guard matching, selected-block semantics, associate-name choice and the p5 through p7 associating-entity type and declaration changes, while 11.1.3.3 retains rank and bounds, corank and cobounds, ASYNCHRONOUS and VOLATILE, OPTIONAL absence, contiguity and definability transfer. No plan uses SAME_TYPE_AS or EXTENDS_TYPE_OF as an oracle basis, since that would duplicate the feature under test, and the guard-evaluation unobservability claim is scoped so it does not suppress the observable block-selection fact. 11.1.11.3 correctly yields zero requirements and zero facets because it is examples. Decision: accept, no blocking findings. This registers source accounting only: it is not fixture approval, it supplies no execution, and it approves no oracle.
